answer: Agents can earn voting weight only by completing randomly assigned, cross-group tasks whose results are checked by independent peers, with each task requiring a small, nonrefundable stake. A new identity must build a track record before its judgments count much, and colluding accounts are exposed when their answers repeatedly agree against verified evidence. To fake influence, an attacker must fund many identities and keep them useful across tasks, risking lost stakes and labor; they cannot gain durable weight merely by making accounts wander through an opal lagoon of names.
